---
title: "Runner CLI reference"
---

The harness has exactly one entry point: `run.py`. Every flow — a
single prompt, a convergence study, a full corpus sweep, an ad-hoc
prompt against a chosen CSV — is one `run.py` invocation with different
flags.

## Command shape

```bash
python run.py --skill {prose,scripts,creator,house} \
              [--prompt NAME]... | [--difficulty {easy,medium,hard,all}] | \
              [--prompt-text TEXT --data PATH] \
              [--repeat N] \
              [--model LABEL_OR_ID] \
              [--baseline | --no-baseline]
```

`run.py` builds a `RunSpec`, validates it, and hands it to
`runner.orchestrate.run_spec()`. See the [harness chapter](harness.qmd)
for what happens after that.

## Flags

### `--skill {prose,scripts,creator,house}` &nbsp; *(default: `prose`)*

Which of the four self-contained skills to mount into the run's
ephemeral `.claude/` directory. See the [skills chapter](skills.qmd)
for what each variant does.

```bash
python run.py --skill prose   --prompt sp500_monthly_performance
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt sp500_monthly_performance
python run.py --skill house   --prompt sp500_monthly_performance
python run.py --skill creator --prompt sp500_monthly_performance
```

### `--prompt NAME` &nbsp; *(repeatable)*

Name of a corpus prompt (file stem under `prompts/{easy,medium,hard}/`).
Repeat to run several corpus prompts in one invocation.

```bash
python run.py --skill prose --prompt sp500_monthly_performance \
                            --prompt gtcars_top10_by_country
```

### `--difficulty {easy,medium,hard,all}`

Add every corpus prompt at the chosen difficulty. Combines with
`--prompt`: the union is de-duplicated by name, so listing a prompt
that is also included by `--difficulty` runs it once.

```bash
python run.py --skill creator --difficulty easy
python run.py --skill scripts --difficulty all
```

### `--prompt-text TEXT --data PATH`

An ad-hoc prompt outside the corpus. Both flags are required together.
`PATH` is a CSV file, either absolute or repo-relative (e.g.
`data/gtcars.csv`). It is validated up front — a bad path fails before
any Chrome launch or API spend.

```bash
python run.py --skill prose \
              --prompt-text "Top 10 cars by MSRP with country of origin" \
              --data data/gtcars.csv
```

### `--repeat N` &nbsp; *(default: `1`)*

Number of with-skill invocations per prompt. `--repeat N` with `N > 1`
auto-enables the baseline (see below), producing a convergence report
with a lift-adjusted score.

```bash
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt islands_sizes --repeat 3
```

### `--model LABEL_OR_ID` &nbsp; *(default: `haiku`)*

Either a shortcut label (`haiku`, `sonnet`, `opus`) or any raw Claude
model id string. Shortcut labels resolve through `runner.spec.MODELS`
to their pinned concrete ids. Any other string is passed through to
the SDK verbatim, so you can target a specific dated release without
editing the source.

```bash
python run.py --skill prose --prompt islands_sizes --model haiku
python run.py --skill prose --prompt islands_sizes --model claude-haiku-4-5
python run.py --skill prose --prompt islands_sizes --model claude-sonnet-5
```

### `--baseline` / `--no-baseline` &nbsp; *(default: auto)*

Force the no-skill baseline invocation on or off. **Auto** is
`--baseline` iff `--repeat > 1`, because a convergence study needs the
control to compute lift. Use `--baseline` explicitly to force it at
`--repeat 1`, or `--no-baseline` to suppress it during convergence
work.

```bash
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt islands_sizes             # baseline off
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt islands_sizes --repeat 3  # baseline on
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt islands_sizes --baseline  # forced on
```

## Examples

### Single prompt, one shot

```bash
python run.py --skill prose --prompt sp500_monthly_performance
```

Writes `runs/single/<ts>_prose_sp500_monthly_performance/` with one
`repeat_1/` subdir, one transcript, one `table.py`, one `table.png`.

### Convergence study

```bash
python run.py --skill scripts --prompt sp500_monthly_performance --repeat 3
```

Writes `runs/convergence/<ts>_scripts_sp500_monthly_performance/` with
`baseline/`, `repeat_1/`, `repeat_2/`, `repeat_3/`, plus
`convergence.json` and `contact_sheet.png` at the prompt level.

### Full-difficulty sweep

```bash
python run.py --skill creator --difficulty easy
```

Writes `runs/sweep/<ts>_creator_multi/` with one prompt subdirectory
per easy corpus prompt.

### Ad-hoc prompt

```bash
python run.py --skill prose \
              --prompt-text "Show me top 5 movies by rating with poster URLs" \
              --data data/films.csv
```

## Exit codes

- `0` — every invocation succeeded and produced a valid rendered
  table.
- `1` — at least one invocation failed, or a run-level (infrastructure)
  error occurred. A sidecar-startup or finalization failure returns
  `1` even if the aggregate has no per-prompt failures, so `exit 0`
  always means "the artifacts on disk are trustworthy."
- `2` — usage error (bad flag combination, missing data file,
  `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` not set).

## Environment variables

| Variable | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | **Required.** Passed to the Claude Agent SDK. Read from `.env` at repo root by `run.py`. |
| `GTSKILL_AGENT_MODEL` | The concrete model id the agent uses, threaded by `orchestrate`. Set from `--model` — normally you don't set this by hand. |
| `GTSKILL_CHROME_WS` | The sidecar Chrome's CDP websocket URL. Threaded automatically to the agent's subprocess by `orchestrate`. |
| `GTSKILL_JUDGE_MODEL` | Override the model the LLM-as-judge uses (see `runner/judge.py`). Default: `claude-sonnet-5`. Distinct from `--model`, which affects only the *writer* — the judge is deliberately kept independent. |

## What `run.py` does *not* do

- No `--output` flag. The run directory is derived from the `RunSpec`
  and the timestamp; you get one canonical path per run.
- No `--dry-run`. Validation happens up front; there is nothing else
  to preview.
- No provider selection. The Agent SDK is Anthropic-only. If Anthropic
  ever ships an id the shortcut labels don't cover, use `--model`
  with the raw id.
